value.title: Multiletter Marton support search
value.objective: Determine whether multiletter Marton coding can strictly improve the current half-skew BSSC achievable rate, and rigorously characterize the super-input support and auxiliary structure required by any such improvement.
value.currentStateSummary: Two structural pruning results now constrain the multiletter Marton search. Conditional on the Geng–Jog–Nair–Wang theorem equating binary-input Marton private-message sum-rate with randomized time division, every finite two-letter half-skew BSSC law supported on at most two super-input symbols has sum-rate below 0.615 bits; relative to the supplied product randomized-time-division benchmark, any strict improvement must therefore use at least three symbols. Independently, for every finite receiver-skew broadcast channel T and every n, the Marton supremum over laws whose coordinate packets (U_i,V_i,X_i) are independent conditioned on the common W equals nM_T, even though W may induce unconditional coordinate correlation. Thus any strict half-skew BSSC gain must be genuinely nonfactorizable conditioned on W under every exact chosen coordinate-packet decomposition to which this theorem applies. For arbitrary tuple laws, an exact decomposition-relative total-correlation ledger supplies a necessary strict correlation-balance inequality for a gain. The ledger is noncanonical, constant padding does not make it intrinsically useful, and the inequality is not sufficient. Three- and four-symbol, conditionally coupled laws remain open, as do unrestricted Marton additivity, binary-input tightness, and exact capacity.
value.localResidualSummary: Analyze three- and four-symbol super-input supports with genuinely nonfactorizable cross-use satellite and input dependence. Apply the decomposition-relative correlation ledger across mathematically useful coordinate packetizations, and seek stronger constraints capable of excluding or constructing laws satisfying its necessary inequality. Independently verify or replace the assumed binary-input Marton-equals-randomized-time-division theorem and any supplied numerical benchmark. The remaining work must distinguish restricted conditional-product additivity from unrestricted Marton additivity and from any capacity conclusion.

value.title: Canonical problem
value.currentStateSummary: Four complementary directions are established. Genuine deterministic finite-block private-message codes induce approximate dependence balance, a fixed encoder-coordinate map, and four compatible rate rows, while an explicit nonbinary witness obstructs the specified coarse entropy and finite copy-lemma route; fixed-cardinality auxiliaries and exact BSSC posterior consistency remain unresolved. The separately relaxed UV scalars tensorize, with receiver-skew symmetry giving equality of the branchwise and averaged scalars and half-skew BSSC product values n(2h_2(1/4)-5/4), but these scalars do not establish capacity. Conditional on the exact encoded Gohari–Liu–Nair Theorem 9 premise, the private-message specialization yields C_sum≤inf_{G,K}B(G,K); compact receiver-curve approximation, finite-grid reduction, row-stability bounds, exact Q0 coercivity, and one fixed-pair weak-duality certificate conditionally giving C_sum≤0.369296945969202842443 are available, while premise authentication, unrelaxed convergence, receiver optimality, and matching achievability remain open. In the multiletter Marton direction, conditional on the assumed Geng–Jog–Nair–Wang binary-input theorem, all two-letter laws supported on at most two super-input symbols are excluded from improving the supplied benchmark. Independently, conditional-product Marton architectures have exactly additive supremum nM_T on every finite receiver-skew channel, so a strict half-skew BSSC gain must use conditionally nonfactorizable coordinate packets. Arbitrary tuple decompositions obey an exact but noncanonical total-correlation ledger whose strict correlation-balance inequality is necessary, not sufficient, for gain. Three- and four-symbol conditionally coupled laws remain unexcluded, and neither restricted additivity result establishes unrestricted Marton additivity, a capacity bound, or the exact BSSC capacity.
value.localResidualSummary: Authenticate or independently prove the external converse premises. Convert compact receiver-curve approximation and relaxed-row stability into an unrelaxed converse limit by controlling active rate-free constraints, boundary behavior, and near-optimal feasibility margins; strengthen receiver coercivity and assess optimality of the certified fixed pair. Derive exact binary-BSSC posterior and multiletter constraints for genuine code-induced laws while retaining coupling absent from the additive relaxed UV scalars. In the achievability direction, analyze three- and four-symbol, conditionally nonfactorizable two-letter Marton laws, use the decomposition-relative correlation ledger where it provides effective pruning, and independently justify any theorem or numerical benchmark used. Exact capacity still requires closing the converse gap and supplying a matching achievable rate.

value.title: Conditional-product Marton additivity and decomposition-relative correlation ledger
value.statement: Let T be a finite receiver-skew two-receiver broadcast channel and M_T its one-letter private-message Marton supremum. For every n≥1, the supremum on T^{⊗n} over finite laws P(w,u^n,v^n,x^n)=P(w)∏_i P_i(u_i,v_i,x_i|w), with aggregate U=U^n and V=V^n, is exactly nM_T. The common W is arbitrary and may induce unconditional coordinate correlation. Hence a strict multiletter gain for the half-skew BSSC cannot have this conditional-product factorization under any exact chosen coordinate-packet decomposition to which the theorem applies. More generally, for any finite tuple law with a chosen decomposition U=(U_i), V=(V_i) over the product channel, let P^(i) be the (W,U_i,V_i,X_i) marginal, TC(A^n|C)=Σ_i H(A_i|C)-H(A^n|C), G_UY=Σ_i H(Y_i|U_i,W)-H(Y^n|U^n,W), G_VZ=Σ_i H(Z_i|V_i,W)-H(Z^n|V^n,W), and G_UV=Σ_i H(U_i|V_i,W)-H(U^n|V^n,W). Then the exact decomposition-relative identity is L_{1/2,T^{⊗n}}(P)-Σ_i L_{1/2,T}(P^(i))=TC(U^n|W)+G_UY+G_VZ-G_UV-(1/2)[TC(Y^n|W)+TC(Y^n)+TC(Z^n|W)+TC(Z^n)]. Consequently, for receiver-skew T, any law giving a strict gain over nM_T must make the left residual positive and therefore satisfy the corresponding strict correlation-balance inequality. This inequality is only necessary. Constant padding always provides a tuple representation, but the ledger and its pruning value depend on the noncanonical chosen decomposition. These conclusions do not establish unrestricted Marton additivity, binary-input tightness, a capacity bound, or the exact half-skew BSSC capacity.
scopeQualifications: The additivity theorem applies only to finite receiver-skew two-receiver broadcast channels and to laws whose chosen coordinate packets factor conditionally on the actual common auxiliary W; W may still correlate coordinates unconditionally.
A strict-gain law must fail the conditional-product factorization for every exact chosen coordinate-packet decomposition to which the theorem applies.
For arbitrary tuple laws, the residual identity and correlation-balance condition are relative to the chosen aggregate coordinate decomposition and are noncanonical.
Constant padding supplies a tuple representation but does not make the resulting ledger canonical or necessarily useful for pruning.
The strict correlation-balance inequality is a necessary condition for a gain, not a sufficient condition.
The result does not establish unrestricted Marton additivity, binary-input tightness, a capacity bound, or the exact half-skew BSSC capacity.

proofs: Receiver-skew reflection exchanges the receiver and satellite roles, making the affine Marton supremum symmetric in its weight. Mixing any candidate with its reflected partner inside an enlarged common auxiliary proves M_T=L_{1/2,T} without a minimax or attainment assumption.

For a conditional-product law, conditioning on W makes the coordinate satellite/output packets independent. The three satellite terms therefore add exactly, while entropy subadditivity bounds each common-output mutual information by its coordinate sum. Applying the one-letter bound coordinatewise gives the upper bound nM_T.

Independent copies of an arbitrary epsilon-optimal one-letter law form an admissible conditional-product law whose complete Marton functional is n times the one-letter value. Letting epsilon decrease to zero proves the reverse inequality without assuming that the one-letter supremum is attained.

For arbitrary tuple laws, direct entropy expansion of the common, private, and penalty differences yields the displayed total-correlation residual identity. Comparing a strict Marton gain with M_T=L_{1/2,T} and the coordinate bounds forces positivity of that residual and hence the strict correlation-balance inequality.
methods: Receiver-skew symmetrization of the Marton functional
Conditional entropy additivity and common-output entropy subadditivity
computations: The submitted deterministic checker verifies the exact rational half-skew BSSC receiver relabeling, mechanically checks the conditional-product satellite identities and common-term bounds on fixed-seed finite examples, checks independent-copy equality of the complete Marton functional, and evaluates both sides of the exact residual identity on correlated tuple laws.
tools: The submitted Python standard-library verifier provides finite-alphabet corroboration of the analytic entropy identities and receiver-skew specialization; it does not exhaust arbitrary alphabets or certify an optimizing law.

placementAudit.rationale: The accepted claim directly advances the existing multiletter Marton support-search objective by excluding the conditional-product architecture and supplying a reusable necessary ledger for the remaining correlated search. Its additivity theorem and residual identity form one coherent reusable result with a shared proof interface. No new durable program, move, split, merge, or retirement is warranted; the affected leaf and its root ancestor are updated holistically.
